consentSettings.intro: Each consent is a record with the version of the document it refers to and the time. Nothing here edits a record: giving or withdrawing adds a new one.
consentSettings.draft: {documents}. The wording has not been approved and may change; a record carries the version it refers to.
consentSettings.stateCaption: The latest record for each purpose
consentSettings.whatsappNotOffered: Set for each client business, not for the firm.
consentSettings.requiredNote: Terms of service, the privacy notice and processing of the business profile are what the service runs on. Withdrawing them ends the service, so it is a data rights request:
consentSettings.outdated: Given for an earlier version; the current one is {current}.
consentSettings.historyCaption: Your consent records, oldest first. They are append-only: a withdrawal is a new record, and earlier records stay as they were.
consentSettings.emptyTitle: No consent recorded for you yet
consentSettings.emptyBody: Nothing is on file for you. The terms, the privacy notice and profile processing are asked for when you get started.
consentSettings.emptyBodyNoStep: Nothing is on file for you. Reminders and analytics can be given above.
consentSettings.recordsWithdraw: This adds a record for {purpose} with granted false, the notice version {notice} of the consent it withdraws, the source web_onboarding (the identity service has no settings source), you as the recorder, the sentence below as evidence, and the time. Earlier records stay as they are.
consentSettings.recordsGive: This adds a record for {purpose} with granted true, the notice version {notice}, the source web_onboarding (the identity service has no settings source), you as the recorder, the sentence below as evidence, and the time.
consentSettings.numberWithdrawHelp: With the country code, starting with +. The number is opted out on the notification service, so reminders to it stop. Leave it empty to record the withdrawal only; the number can also reply STOP.
consentSettings.numberGiveHelp: With the country code, starting with +. The notification service opts this number in once the consent is recorded.
consentSettings.error.purpose: This consent is not changed on this page.
consentSettings.error.change: Choose to give or to withdraw the consent.
consentSettings.error.optOutFailed: Nothing was recorded: the number could not be opted out.
consentSettings.error.recordAfterOptOut: The number is opted out, but the withdrawal is not recorded yet. Try again.
consentSettings.error.optInFailed: Your consent is recorded, but the number is not opted in yet. Try again.
consentSettings.error.closed: Consents cannot be given while the legal documents are drafts; nothing was recorded. Withdrawing a consent always works.
consentSettings.done.alreadyWithdrawn: {purpose} was not given, so nothing new was recorded.
consentSettings.done.alreadyGiven: {purpose} was already given for the current version, so nothing new was recorded.
notifications.intro: Whether reminders reach a WhatsApp number or an email address, in which language, and the quiet hours in Indian Standard Time when they are held. Each preference is kept by the notification service for one number or address.
notifications.recipientNote: The identity service does not return your own number and address yet, so name them here. The page remembers them on this device only, until you sign out.
notifications.recipientHelp.whatsapp: With the country code, starting with +.
notifications.recipientHelp.email: The address the reminders go to.
notifications.consentGiven: Your consent to {purpose} is on file.
notifications.consentNotGiven: Your consent to {purpose} is not on file, so reminders cannot be switched on here.
notifications.consentMissing: Give the consent first; the service opts a recipient in only once it is recorded. Switching reminders off and changing the language or the quiet hours work without it.
notifications.emailNote: The notification service does not deliver email yet: its email channel is not connected. A preference is still recorded and applies once it is.
notifications.notRecordedTitle: Nothing is recorded for this recipient
notifications.notRecorded: The notification service sends nothing to a recipient that is not opted in. The form starts from the service's defaults: English, and quiet hours from 21:00 to 08:00 IST.
notifications.languageHelp: The languages the service has message templates in for this channel.
notifications.quietHelp: A reminder due in this window is held and sent when it ends. A window may run past midnight; the same start and end means no quiet hours.
notifications.error.emailMissing: Enter the address the reminders go to.
notifications.error.email: Enter an email address, such as name@example.com.
notifications.error.language: Choose one of the languages listed.
notifications.error.time: Enter a time as HH:MM on the 24-hour clock.
notifications.error.consentMissing: Your consent to {purpose} is not on file, so reminders were not switched on. Give it on the Consents page, or choose not to send reminders.
notifications.error.consentMissingField: Reminders can be switched on once your consent is on file.

documents.open.noList: A list of the documents each source has fetched arrives with the source manager. Until then, a document is opened by its id: from a review item, a relation candidate or the pipeline's logs.
documents.view.intro: The document as the rulebook stores it, clause by clause. The text is shown exactly as parsed.
documents.view.noClauses: The rulebook holds no clauses for this document.

documents.highlight.clause: Clause {ref} is marked, as the link asked.

documents.highlight.missingTitle: The clause is not in this document
documents.highlight.missing: The link asked to mark clause {clauseId}, which this document does not hold. Nothing is marked.

rulebookWrites.reviewsDisabled: The rulebook does not accept decisions

rulebookWrites.flagOffDetail: Turn on the {flag} flag for this tenant to send decisions to the rulebook.
ruleVersions.intro: Every version of the rulebook's rules: those in force on a date, and those moving through review, drafts included. A version is in force only once it is published, from its effective date.
ruleVersions.asOfHelp: The rulebook lists the published or superseded version of each rule whose period covers this date.
ruleVersions.ruleInvalid: This is not a rule key (lower-case letters, digits and underscores).
ruleVersions.fixFilter: Nothing is listed until the filter is corrected.
ruleVersions.mode.inForce: Versions in force on {date} for {rule}, by rule key, as the rulebook's as-of read gives them.
ruleVersions.mode.status: Versions in the status {status} for {rule}, read from each rule's versions, by rule key.
ruleVersions.mode.all: Every version of {rule}, in any status, read from each rule's versions, by rule key.
ruleVersions.empty.inForceTitle: No version is in force on {date}
ruleVersions.empty.inForceBody: A version is in force only once an analyst has published it through the review workflow, and only from its effective date.
ruleVersions.empty.statusBody: None of the rules listed has a version in this status now.
ruleVersions.caption: {count} versions on this page
ruleVersion.intro: Version {version} of the rule {rule}, as the rulebook holds it.
ruleVersion.notReviewedBody: No analyst has completed a review round for this version. Check every fact on this page against the cited instrument, answer the open questions and cite the clauses it rests on before it is approved.
ruleVersion.highImpactYes: Yes: publishing needs two different approvers
ruleVersion.obligationUnread: The obligation template is not in a shape this page can read; it is shown as stored below.
ruleVersion.dueInDays: {days} days after the event that triggers it
ruleVersion.noQuestions: The version carries no open question.
ruleVersion.asStored: The condition, obligation, recurrence and source as stored
ruleVersion.asStoredLabel: The version's mappings as the rulebook stores them
ruleVersion.spec.anyOf: At least one of these holds:
ruleVersion.spec.unreadable: A part of the condition this page cannot read, as stored:
ruleVersion.spec.ontologyMissing: The ontology could not be read, so the values below are shown as stored, without their labels or meanings.
ruleVersion.spec.none: The version states no condition yet.
ruleVersion.workflow.heading: Publish workflow
ruleVersion.workflow.oneApprover: A version goes from draft to review, is approved, then published. This one needs one approver.
ruleVersion.workflow.twoApprovers: A version goes from draft to review, is approved, then published. This one is high impact: it needs two different approvers.
ruleVersion.workflow.noSteps: No further step: a superseded or withdrawn version does not change.
ruleVersion.workflow.unknownStep: Choose a step of the workflow.
ruleVersion.workflow.noteTooLong: A note has at most {max} characters.
ruleVersion.workflow.reasonRequired: Give a reason of at least {min} characters.
ruleVersion.workflow.unknownVersion: This is not a rule version id.
ruleVersion.round.unknown: The rulebook reports the approvers of a review round in its answer to each step; its version read does not carry them yet, so they show here after a step.
ruleVersion.round.needsAnother: It needs a second approver: a different analyst.
ruleVersion.round.none: No approval in this round yet.
ruleVersion.outcome.submitted: Submitted for review: a new review round started.
ruleVersion.outcome.submittedHighImpact: Submitted for review as high impact: a new review round started, and it needs two different approvers.
ruleVersion.outcome.approvalRecorded: Your approval is recorded: {count} of {required} approvals. The version stays in review until the round is complete.
ruleVersion.outcome.approved: Approved: {count} of {required} approvals. The version can be published.
ruleVersion.outcome.published: Published. It replaces {replaced} versions and moves {moved} due dates, as its relations say.
ruleVersion.outcome.returned: Returned to draft: the round's approvals no longer count.
ruleVersion.dialog.title: {step}: version {version}
ruleVersion.dialog.submit: Records on the rulebook that you submitted this version, with the time and your note, and starts a new review round.
ruleVersion.dialog.approve: Records your approval in this round on the rulebook, with the time and your note. One analyst approves a round once.
ruleVersion.dialog.publish: Publishes the version from its effective date, applies its relations and writes the rule events, with the time and your note.
ruleVersion.dialog.return: Sends the version back to draft: the round's approvals stop counting and it needs review again. The reason is recorded with the step.
ruleVersion.dialog.withdraw: Withdraws the published version from today and writes the rule's withdrawal event. The reason is recorded with the step.
ruleVersion.dialog.noteHelp: Kept with the step on the rulebook; at most {max} characters.
ruleVersion.dialog.highImpact: High impact: publishing needs two different approvers
ruleVersion.dialog.highImpactHelp: Once set, a later submission keeps it.
ruleVersion.dialog.highImpactKept: This version is already high impact; a submission keeps it.
citations.heading: Citations
citations.intro: The clauses the version rests on, each with the words of it the rule takes and the rulebook's verification: the quote must closely match its clause and carry no number, form code or month the clause lacks.
citations.emptyBody: A version is published only with at least one citation, every one verified. Cite the clauses it rests on while it is a draft.
citations.caption: {count} citations
citations.clauseUnread: The clause could not be read.
citations.draftOnly: Citations are added only while the version is a draft: return it to draft to cite another clause.
citations.saved: Stored. New citations: {added}; already cited: {unchanged}. Every quote was found in its clause.
citations.failuresLead: The rulebook could not find these quotes in their clauses, so nothing was stored:
citations.form.heading: Cite clauses
citations.form.intro: Give each clause's id (from the document viewer or the clause search) and the words of it the rule rests on. The rulebook stores every row or none.
citations.form.label: Cite clauses
citations.form.quoteHelp: The clause's words, as written; at most {max} characters.
citations.form.clauseMalformed: This is not a clause id (a UUID).
citations.form.clauseUnknown: The rulebook holds no clause with this id.
citations.form.quoteRequired: Enter the words of the clause the rule rests on.
citations.form.quoteTooLong: A quote has at most {max} characters.
citations.form.noneGiven: Add at least one citation: a clause id and a quote.
relations.heading: Relations
relations.intro: What this version says about other versions and entities, which takes effect when it is published, and what other versions say about it.
relations.toEmpty: No version states a relation to this one.
entities.meaning.resolved: The name is the canonical name or an alias of one entity.
entities.meaning.ambiguous: The name is an alias of more than one entity: pick the one meant.
entities.meaning.not_found: No entity has this name or alias. An entity is created only when an analyst decides a group of mentions on the entity review queue.
entities.meaning.unqualified: A section or rule named without its statute (written section@statute) cannot name one entity.
entities.meaning.empty: Nothing is left of the name once it is normalised.
entities.resolve.intro: What the rulebook makes of a name, the way it aligns a mention it finds in a document: the name is normalised, then matched against the canonical names and aliases of that type. No route lists the entities, so this is the way to one.
entities.resolve.name: Name
entities.resolve.nameTooLong: A name has at most {max} characters.
entities.resolve.emptyTitle: Resolve a name to an entity
entities.resolve.emptyBody: Choose the type and give the name as a document writes it; the rulebook says whether one entity has it, several, or none.
entities.page.intro: A canonical {type} entity of the rulebook's knowledge graph, with the clauses that mention it and the relations that point at it.
entities.fact.name: Canonical name
entities.page.clausesIntro: Newest document first, the mentions marked. With a date, only documents published by then, and each clause says whether the rule it states is out of force on that date.
entities.page.asOfForm: Show the clauses as of a date
entities.page.asOfHelp: Optional; leave empty for every document.
entities.page.noClausesBody: The rulebook holds no aligned mention of this entity yet.
entities.page.noClausesBodyAsOf: No document published by {date} mentions this entity.
entities.page.outOfForce: Its rule is out of force on this date
entities.page.relationsIntro: Relations rule versions state about this entity, drafts' included, each with its evidence clause.
entities.page.noRelations: No rule version states a relation to this entity.
search.intro: Find the clauses of the rulebook's documents that a few words point to. The words are posted, never put in the address.
search.legs: The rulebook runs two searches and fuses their ranks: a full-text one over the clauses' words and a vector one over their embeddings. Each hit carries its rank in each and the fused score. This page sends the words without an embedding, so the vector search does not run from here and no hit has a vector rank.
search.form.label: Search the clauses
search.form.textHelp: As a question or a phrase from a document; up to 2000 characters.
search.form.asOfHelp: Optional: only documents published on or before this date.
search.form.docTypes: Document types (none ticked means every type)
search.form.textRequired: Enter the words to search for.
search.form.regulatorTooLong: A regulator has at most {max} characters.
search.form.docTypeUnknown: Choose document types from the list.
search.form.countUnknown: Choose how many hits from the list.
search.results.heading: Results
search.results.emptyBody: No clause of the documents the filters keep holds these words. Try other words, or fewer filters.

graph.form.versionUnknown: The rulebook holds no rule version with this id.
